_comment_: Template D — Stop verification via prompt-type hook (NOT a script — paste this block into settings.json under hooks.Stop)
_comment_2_: Why prompt-type? Stop verification needs SEMANTIC judgment ('did Claude actually verify?'), not pattern matching. LLM evaluates and returns {ok: bool, reason?: string}.
_comment_3_: Cost note: each Stop fires a small LLM call (~1-2K tokens). Long sessions accumulate. Consider gating with `if` to only fire when Edit/Write happened in session.

hooks.prompt:
Evaluate whether Claude truly verified the task before stopping. Check the last 10 turns:
1) Was test or build executed for code changes? (look for `dotnet test`, `npm test`, `pytest`, etc.)
2) Was read-before-modify followed? (every Edit preceded by Read of same file)
3) Are claims backed by file:line citations?
4) For docs/schema changes: was schema alignment confirmed?

Return strict JSON:
  {"ok": true} — verification looks adequate
  {"ok": false, "reason": "missing step X"} — Claude must continue

Do not be overly strict; minor cosmetic edits or read-only tasks do not require running tests.

_alternative_agent_type_._comment_: If prompt-type isn't thorough enough, use agent-type which can read files. Slower but more reliable.
